csid_cog.title: Memory and thinking check
csid_cog.intro: Ask the person each question in the language they are most comfortable with. Do not give hints. Mark what they actually said or did.

source.citation: Prince M, et al. A brief dementia screener suitable for use by non-specialists in resource poor settings: the cross-cultural derivation and validation of the brief Community Screening Instrument for Dementia. Int J Geriatr Psychiatry 2011;26(9):899-907.

csid_cog.licence: Items are from the open-access article above (Creative Commons Attribution 2.5; re-use permitted, commercial exploitation not permitted). The parent CSI-D was developed by K. S. Hall and colleagues. Confirm permission and obtain a validated local-language version before any real field use.
csid_cog.wording_status: English administration wording follows the published appendix. No translation is shipped: unvalidated translations of cognitive test items are not acceptable for screening.

items.prompt: First, say: "I am going to tell you three words. Please repeat them and try to remember them: Boat, House, Fish."
items.guide: Repeat the three words until the person can say all three (up to six tries). This step is not scored. You will ask for the words again at the end.

items.prompt: Point to your own elbow and ask: "What do we call this?"
"What do you do with a hammer?"
items.guide: Correct if the answer shows they know its use, for example driving a nail into something.

items.prompt: "Where is the local market or the nearest shop?"
items.guide: Correct if the answer is right for where the person lives.

items.prompt: "What day of the week is it today?"
"What season is it now?"
items.guide: Accept the season name people use locally.

items.prompt: "Please point first to the window and then to the door."
items.guide: Correct only if both are pointed to, in that order.

items.prompt: "Do you remember the three words I told you a few minutes ago?"
items.guide: The words were Boat, House, Fish. Count how many the person recalls without help.

csid_inf.title: Questions for a family member
csid_inf.intro: Ask someone who knows the person well and sees them often, ideally away from the person. Ask about changes compared with how the person used to be.

source.citation: Prince M, et al. Int J Geriatr Psychiatry 2011;26(9):899-907.

csid_inf.licence: Items are from the open-access article above (Creative Commons Attribution 2.5; non-commercial). Confirm permission and obtain a validated local-language version before any real field use.

items.prompt: "Has there been a general decline in their mental functioning?"
"Have you noticed a change in their ability to think and reason?"
"Do they often forget where they have put things?"
"Do they sometimes forget what happened the day before?"
"Do they sometimes forget where they are?"
"Do they have difficulty dressing, such as misplacing buttons or putting clothes on in the wrong order or the wrong way?"
items.guide: If the difficulty is only because of a physical problem (for example arthritis or a weak arm), mark No.

iqcode16.title: Longer family interview
iqcode16.intro: Say: "Think about what they were like 10 years ago and compare it with what they are like now. For each situation, tell me whether they have improved, stayed the same, or got worse." The comparison is always with their own earlier level, not with other people.

source.citation: Jorm AF. A short form of the Informant Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly (IQCODE): development and cross-validation. Psychol Med 1994;24(1):145-153.

iqcode16.licence: The published form states: "There is no copyright on the Short IQCODE." The author asks to be kept informed of research projects that use it.

items.prompt: Remembering things about family and friends, such as occupations, birthdays, addresses
Remembering things that have happened recently
Recalling conversations a few days later
Remembering their own address and telephone number
Remembering what day and month it is
Remembering where things are usually kept
Remembering where to find things which have been put in a different place from usual
Knowing how to work familiar machines around the house
Learning to use a new gadget or machine around the house
Learning new things in general
Following a story in a book or on TV
Making decisions on everyday matters
Handling money for shopping
Handling financial matters, such as the pension or dealing with the bank
Handling other everyday arithmetic problems, such as knowing how much food to buy or how long it is between visits from family or friends
Using their intelligence to understand what is going on and to reason things through

phq2.title: Mood check
phq2.intro: Low mood can look like memory trouble, and the two often occur together. Say: "Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?"

source.citation: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JBW. The Patient Health Questionnaire-2: validity of a two-item depression screener. Med Care 2003;41(11):1284-1292.

phq2.licence: The PHQ family of measures is distributed by its developers for reproduction and use without permission. Verify the current terms at phqscreeners.com before distribution.

items.prompt: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless

rules.status: DRAFT. Not approved for clinical use. A supervising clinician must review every threshold and message before this is used with real people.

csid_combined_max.meaning: cognitive score minus informant score at or below this is a positive screen
csid_combined_max.source: Prince 2011: combined score <5 optimal in India, China, Latin America and Nigeria pilot samples

csid_cog_positive_max.meaning: with no informant, a cognitive score at or below this is a positive screen
csid_cog_positive_max.source: Prince 2011: 4 or less on the cognitive scale 'highly suggestive'

csid_cog_indeterminate_max.meaning: with no informant, cognitive scores above the positive cut-off and up to this value are indeterminate
csid_cog_indeterminate_max.source: Prince 2011: for scores of 5 or 6 an informant interview and reassessment after several months are advised

csid_inf_min.meaning: informant score at or above this is a positive informant screen
csid_inf_min.source: Prince 2011: informant score >1 optimal in all regions except Nigeria

iqcode16_min_x100.meaning: mean Short IQCODE score, times 100, at or above this is a positive screen
iqcode16_min_x100.source: Jorm 2004 review recommends 3.44+ as a screening compromise; community studies range about 3.3 to 3.6

phq2_min.meaning: PHQ-2 total at or above this is a positive depression screen
phq2_min.source: Kroenke 2003: score of 3 or more, sensitivity 83%, specificity 92% for major depression

followup_months.meaning: when to repeat an indeterminate screen
followup_months.source: Prince 2011 says 'after several months'; the exact interval is this project's choice

red_flags.label: Confusion started suddenly, or got much worse over hours or days
red_flags.why: Sudden change is not typical of dementia. It can mean infection, medicine side effects or another illness that needs treatment now.

red_flags.label: New weakness or numbness on one side, face drooping, or new trouble speaking
red_flags.why: These can be signs of a stroke.

red_flags.label: Recent fall or blow to the head, followed by drowsiness or a change in thinking
red_flags.why: Bleeding inside the skull can develop after a head injury.

red_flags.label: Not safe right now: getting lost, not eating or drinking, or signs of neglect or harm
red_flags.why: The person needs help with safety before any memory assessment.

rules.red_flags_basis: project default: general clinical safety-netting, to be reviewed by the supervising clinician

conditions.label: Could not see well enough for the pointing task
Unwell, in pain, or very tired today
Questions were not in the person's first language

URGENT.title: Needs to see a doctor today
URGENT.say: Some of what you have told me needs a doctor to look at it today. This is not about memory loss from ageing. Please go to the nearest health centre or hospital now.

REFER.title: Refer to the clinic for a memory assessment
REFER.say: This check suggests it would be worth having a doctor look more closely at memory and thinking. This is not a diagnosis. Many things can cause these results and some of them are treatable.

FOLLOW_UP.title: Check again
FOLLOW_UP.say: This check did not give a clear answer. We will check again, and it helps if a family member can answer a few questions too.

INCOMPLETE.title: Screening not finished
INCOMPLETE.say: We could not finish the check today. We will come back to complete it.

NO_REFERRAL.title: No referral needed now
NO_REFERRAL.say: This check did not find signs that need a referral now. If you or your family notice memory or thinking getting worse, please ask for another check.

reasons.csid_combined_positive: Memory check and family interview together are in the range that needs assessment
reasons.csid_cog_positive: Memory check score is in the range that needs assessment
reasons.csid_inf_positive: Family member reports changes in the range that needs assessment
reasons.iqcode_positive: Longer family interview shows decline in the range that needs assessment
reasons.csid_cog_indeterminate: Memory check score is borderline and there was no family interview
reasons.informant_concern: Family member reports changes even though the memory check was in the usual range
reasons.nothing_scored: No memory check or family interview was completed

notes.phq2_positive: Mood check is positive. Low mood can cause or worsen memory trouble: tell the clinic, or suggest a primary care visit for mood.
notes.test_conditions: Testing conditions were not ideal, so the memory check score may be lower than the person's real ability.
notes.no_informant: No family member was interviewed. Screening is more accurate with one.

interpretation_limits: A positive screen is not a diagnosis of dementia or Alzheimer's disease.
A negative screen does not rule dementia out.
Published accuracy figures come from research samples that compared people already known to have dementia with healthy controls. Accuracy in routine community use is expected to be lower.
The brief CSI-D was derived from items embedded in a longer interview; its authors state that validity of the stand-alone brief form in routine primary care still needed to be established.
